verdict.root_cause: At 09:51:20 UTC an automated environment update on cartservice introduced a Redis address variable (previously unset, so the service had been using its baked-in default endpoint) pointing at redis-cart:6380 [tr_4f54ca0da4a7]. cartservice was serving AddItem/GetCart/EmptyCart normally at the start of the window and only later entered a loop of failed connection attempts to that exact host and non-default port, with an unhandled exception thrown from RedisCartStore.InitializeAsync/EnsureRedisConnected in Main — i.e. the process never finishes startup and crash-loops rather than degrading [tr_287da123d1d8]. With cartservice unable to serve, every sampled checkout trace fails identically on checkoutservice's outbound hipstershop.CartService/GetCart span, and that ERROR propagates through checkoutservice PlaceOrder into frontend PlaceOrder and the frontend HTTP POST [tr_84ff3bfd8f4d], which matches the observed checkoutservice error ratio peaking near 67% and frontend near 35% (checkout is only a fraction of frontend traffic) [tr_663cc5422f32, tr_a75ec76afef0]. The failing mechanism is the configuration value itself: the endpoint it names is not one a Redis server answers on, and that wrongness is what breaks every cart read. It is not a deploy (no image/version change anywhere, and the three other change queries were empty) and not latency (all failing spans complete in 1–7ms, and the Redis connect never succeeds at all).
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on cartservice's Redis endpoint. (1) Localization: traces show a single, uniform termination point at the CartService/GetCart boundary with checkoutservice's own spans completing normally and no downstream service (payment, currency, shipping, catalog, accounting) ever reached [tr_84ff3bfd8f4d]; productcatalogservice's error ratio is a measured zero across all 61 samples [tr_5238aec71711], and frontend/checkout are propagators whose error ratios are consistent with a cart-path-only failure [tr_a75ec76afef0, tr_663cc5422f32]. (2) Mechanism: cartservice logs place the fault in startup store initialization, not request handling, with the connection never established — ruling out a slow/overloaded Redis and pointing at an unreachable endpoint [tr_287da123d1d8]. (3) Trigger: the only recorded change in the covered window is the cartservice environment mutation naming redis-cart:6380, machine-originated, config-only with no artifact change, landing ~2.5 minutes before the 09:54 pages [tr_4f54ca0da4a7]; frontend, checkoutservice and productcatalogservice change logs are empty [tr_9373afe09afe, tr_e8cbbe4269bd, tr_c6b98ef7dd43]. The variable was previously unset and the service was demonstrably healthy under its prior default, so the newly-written value is the discriminating difference. Classed bad_config rather than bad_deploy because no artifact changed, and rather than dependency_latency because nothing waits — the connect fails and the failing spans return in milliseconds. Remediation is reverting the address (or correcting it to the port Redis actually serves), not a rollback of any image; a restart alone would only re-enter the same crash loop. Note the cartservice metric result contributes nothing about health either way — its absence is a telemetry gap, explicitly not a zero [tr_8f33eb8fc66f].
open_questions: Nothing confirmed what port redis-cart actually listens on. If the platform was in the middle of migrating Redis to 6380 and the server side never landed or is itself down, the cartservice value is 'early' rather than 'wrong', and the correct fix is completing/repairing the Redis side, not reverting the client. No dispatch touched redis-cart directly.

The change-tool budget (4/4) was exhausted before any query covered 09:30-09:44, so a change on any service in that earlier interval — including a redis-cart change — is unverified. All four change results explicitly flag this gap.

Exact onset is unpinned on both sides: the frontend and checkoutservice metric results returned only min/max aggregates, not the per-timestamp series, and the cartservice log query returned only the oldest 8 and newest 32 lines, omitting the 09:51:20 transition. The 09:51:20 -> ~09:54 causal ordering is inferred from the alert times, not directly observed.
No latency percentiles were retrieved for frontend, checkoutservice or cartservice. The traces argue strongly against a latency component, but the metric half of that question is unanswered.

Why the automation wrote this value is unknown — a pipeline template, a policy rollout, or a partially-applied migration. Without that, a config_revert may simply be re-applied by the same automation.

cartservice emits no calls_total series at all for the window [tr_8f33eb8fc66f]. This is consistent with the crash loop but could also be a pre-existing label or scrape problem; it was not resolved, so cartservice's own error/latency behaviour before 09:51:20 rests solely on the eight early log lines.
Blast radius was 12 services with 4 unmeasured edges crossed; only 4 services were examined. Whether any impact outside the checkout path shares this cause or is independent was never tested.
